compiled_state.title: merge-to-main: orchestrator disables GitHub workflow without verifying token has admin scope -> workflow stuck disabled
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 2. Incident Overview

**What happened**: The orchestrator called \`gh workflow disable reconcile-bridge.yml\` and \`gh workflow enable reconcile-bridge.yml\` multiple times during the session. These calls succeeded initially but later failed with HTTP 403 (Resource not accessible by personal access token). The workflow is now stuck in disabled_manually state and the PAT cannot re-enable it because it lacks the Administration permission required by the PUT /actions/workflows/{id}/enable endpoint.

**Expected behavior**: The orchestrator should verify it can both enable AND disable a workflow before disabling it. If the token lacks admin scope, the orchestrator should not disable the workflow — instead it should warn the user that the cron cannot be safely toggled.

**Actual behavior**: The orchestrator disabled the workflow without checking whether it could re-enable it later, leaving the workflow permanently disabled until a human with admin access intervenes via the GitHub UI.
